        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The design in the study is described as a methodology developed to help blind students read music scores without using Braille. The software provides a direct perception of the notes by singing the names of the notes and speaking the names of chords. This approach is primarily utilitarian, focusing on the functional need to help blind individuals learn music. The design was created by specialists (educators and researchers) and incorporates fun elements later, such as singing the names of the notes, to make the learning process more engaging. However, the primary focus is on utility, making it a 'totally utility first' design.
